missions.title: The Glass Meridian
missions.subtitle: Someone is selling the same safe passage to two ships at once.
missions.offer: Dock at Avenor after visiting three different systems and identifying two ship types. No kill-count gate or dependency on another campaign.
missions.story: Avenor has recorded three near-collisions on a supposedly certified medical freight lane. Its navigation buoys agree about position but disagree about time. A missing civilian surveyor is being blamed. The real fault is a contractor selling duplicate reservations and disguising the conflict as pilot error. The commander must recover the survey record, rebuild the timing chain and guide a clinic ship through a corrected lane before deciding how to release the evidence.
missions.playerBriefing: Captain Elara Venn: Our clinic convoy cannot launch while two ships can hold the same reservation. Read the beacons at Renas. Look for the surveyor at Navidor. Bring back evidence before deciding who is at fault.
missions.completionBenefit: A public lane-safety commendation and the selected evidence outcome in regional gossip. No fabricated combat points or automatic ship blueprint. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The missing instant.

missions.title: A Choir Beneath the Static
missions.subtitle: A signal mistaken for a weapon may be a request for help.
missions.offer: After identifying a Larvaal vessel and visiting four systems, speak to Holt at Omdogan in Galaxy 4. This campaign is independent of The Glass Meridian.
missions.story: Mining navigation receivers in Quiet Current are being drowned by repeating Larvaal phase pulses. The pulses contain synchronized gaps, not firing orders. A damaged Larvaal Probe has been trying to locate its dispersed companions while human smugglers imitate the signal to conceal their own traffic. The commander reconstructs the pulses, repairs the probe, exposes the imitation and negotiates a narrow-band rendezvous that lets both fleets navigate safely.
missions.playerBriefing: Captain Tamsin Holt: No one has proved these pulses are an attack. Calibrate your receiver at Lobagom before approaching the source. Agent Mara Vale will compare what you find with the mining relays.
missions.completionBenefit: A resonance-filter fitting, improving identification of this campaign's Larvaal signals. It grants no extra energy capacity, general faction immunity or free ship fabrication. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The silent voice.

missions.title: The Hollow Manifest
missions.subtitle: The cargo exists on paper. The danger is aboard a real ship.
missions.offer: Speak to freight auditor Nia Toren at Narargan in Galaxy 2 after completing one normal commodity sale. No score gate or link to another campaign.
missions.story: A freight mutual is paying claims for industrial cargo that never left its warehouse. Reused seals make innocent captains appear responsible, while the true carrier transports unlisted refinery waste. The commander follows a physical seal through several freighters, rescues the carrier's stranded crew, recovers the original customs register and chooses public disclosure or a restitution tribunal. The witnesses are protected and the cargo fraud is resolved through evidence rather than revenge.
missions.playerBriefing: Nia Toren: Two paid manifests name the same crate, and both captains insist it never reached them. Scan the freighters at Garrivek. If we follow the seal rather than the accusation, we can find where the cargo really went.
missions.completionBenefit: Expense reimbursement is tracked separately; the selected public report or restitution fund appears in local gossip. Existing legal status is never reset. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The inward mark.

missions.title: The Borrowed Voice
missions.subtitle: Someone has learned to speak with the rescue network's voice.
missions.offer: At Taledea in Galaxy 3, after visiting five different systems, speak to rescue coordinator Sera Dain. No combat score, prior campaign, purchased scanner or military fitting is required.
missions.story: Rescue tenders in the Taledea cluster are answering empty distress calls while real casualties wait. A covert salvage syndicate has enrolled a second operator under a dispatcher's credentials and is selling rescue movements to ambushers. Dispatcher Neris Sol discovered the duplicate account and went into hiding. The commander validates the false calls, equips an independent verifier, brings Sol to safety and chooses between publicly revoking the compromised key or quietly drawing a syndicate observer to an empty decoy. Both routes recover an authenticated access record. The commander exposes the infiltrating account and restores the rescue channels.
missions.playerBriefing: SERA DAIN: Our tenders have been called to three empty wrecks. Meanwhile, a real casualty waited alone. Compare the relay records at Ilasaeli. Do not broadcast patient locations; someone may be listening with one of our own keys.
missions.completionBenefit: The rescue network resumes service. The selected open-revocation or protected-witness outcome appears in regional gossip. No legal-status reset, artificial kill points, free hull or general faction immunity. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The unclaimed channel.

missions.title: The Shattered Wake
missions.subtitle: A station can stop a weapon volley. Can it survive an entire broken orbit?
missions.offer: At Loalaila in Galaxy 6, after visiting three systems, speak to Controller Edda Rell. No kill-count gate or prior campaign. The loaned coupler needs one tonne of hold; standard flight, targeting and weapons are sufficient.
missions.story: An abandoned orbital mass driver above Aermiori has restarted during an automated survey. Its spoil stream intersects a fractured moonlet, sending a long train of large bodies and dense gravel towards Spindle Anchorage. The station can discharge the firepower of an ordinary ship, but successive heavy impacts can exhaust its shields before they recover. The commander measures the approaching train, shuts down the driver and helps build either a tug-deflection array or a fragment-catching screen. The commander can visit neighbouring systems with a verified warning and recruit their available tugs, interception patrols and evacuation craft. During the passage, the commander redirects marked threats and clears a route for rescue craft. Afterwards, survivors and the flight records are taken to Loalaila, where an inquiry determines what happened and how to protect the next orbital settlement.
missions.playerBriefing: RELL: Spindle Anchorage can absorb a ship's weapons all day. These are moving mountains and a wake of gravel. We need to change their paths before they share the same few seconds against the shields. Survey the outer watchers at Aermiori. We have time to prepare; I will not arm the operation until you confirm readiness.
missions.completionBenefit: The completed relief and inquiry earns the base 1,800 CR. Add 6,000 CR if Spindle Anchorage survives, or 3,000 CR if the station is lost but all registered evacuees reach Shelter Dock; no bonus for other station-loss outcomes. All outcomes require the later relief and inquiry, not merely waiting for an explosion. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The curve before the fall.
missions.branchPolicy: Choose tug-deflection or fragment-screen once. The selected deploy-defence variant changes the mitigation available during the same debris passage. Afterwards, all station outcomes continue through rescue, relief and inquiry. The choice alone never guarantees survival.
missions.rewardPolicy: At the confirmed inquiry terminal, pay the 1,800 CR base plus exactly one bonus from completionBonusesCR, using the persisted authoritative hazard outcome. Commit that sum, completion and clue atomically under one final-payment receipt. No payment or clue is earned solely by a station loss, an NPC interception or leaving the system. Do not clear legal status or grant combat kills for rocks or environmental station loss. Commit the clue and terminal reward receipt atomically; a pending optional fitting does not delay the clue.
interactionNotes: Use normal targeting and scans, contextual Confirm actions and the shared help controls. Esc cancels a dialog without choosing an operation or arming the timer.

The impulse coupler uses one tonne between collection and completed defence deployment. It is loaned without a fee and installed into the final node in one atomic transfer. No salvage, record or clue requires spare hold.

After the watcher survey, optional contacts at Iraeth, Reilieli and Siamaeth can dispatch available tugs, patrol ships and rescue haulers. The mission log shows routes, warning receipts, offers, departures and arrival estimates. Warn any subset before arming; late visits remain possible but do not pause an active passage.

Preparation has no deadline. Before arming, display the operation, all targets, 15-minute passage clock, shield reserve, impact load, structural integrity, rescue manifest and safe breakup range. Confirm at the final deployment starts the advertised clock; cancelling does not.

After arming, the active simulation clock continues during docking, radio dialogs and interstellar departure. Explicit game pause, automatic background pause and system sleep freeze it. Save/load resumes the same elapsed passage, impact queue and rescue manifest; it does not replay impacts or reset the station.
The station can be genuinely destroyed by the accumulated asteroid impacts. Rescue and the inquiry use Shelter Dock and Loalaila, so loss of Spindle Anchorage cannot remove the remaining objectives.

A lost rescue tender can be replaced by a new crew and hull. Persist survivors already safe at Shelter Dock. Do not recreate dead evacuees, clone a tender's passenger manifest or award an arrival for a culled ship.

stationPolicy.singleShipWeapons: Ordinary single-ship weapon fire cannot penetrate the station shields or reduce structural integrity. Ship fire never counts as an asteroid impact.
stationPolicy.kineticDamage: Authoritative collisions by physical asteroids and fragments draw from a recharging shield reserve. Unabsorbed load damages structural integrity. Repeated impacts can destroy a station.
stationPolicy.units: Independent normalised gameplay loads; physical impact-energy conversion and station-size budgets require runtime balancing.
stationPolicy.duplicatePolicy: A collision receipt combines encounter and collider identity; process it once. Splitting conserves the parent's mass, momentum and total kinetic-energy budget. Invalidate the parent and give children new identities; never count the parent and its children as separate intact masses.

hazardRules.populations: A primary body, six secondary bodies and eighty individually tracked or deterministically clustered fragments. Broad bands arrive over the passage; the exact source-free trajectory recipe is fixed and saved at arming.
hazardRules.mitigation: Tug-deflection pushes marked large bodies onto predicted miss paths but leaves most gravel. Fragment-screen catches a finite share of the gravel while leaving large bodies for the player and tugs. Both are viable with normal controls; tune difficulty through original trials.
hazardRules.breakup: Weapon damage to a rock may break it up without removing its momentum or danger. Show predicted fragment trajectories and a warning inside 35 km. Outside that range a verified interception can spread fragments onto miss paths; distance alone is not a successful interception.
hazardRules.evacuation: At arming, register the full station population eligible for evacuation, including people not yet aboard a launch. At a warned shield threshold, launch available craft before collapse. Track each registered person as aboard, in an escape capsule, rescued, safe at Shelter Dock or lost. Reinforcement haulers add real transport capacity, never new passengers or an automatic success.
hazardRules.loss: Persist real station loss, disable docking and services there, show wreckage and update charts and gossip. Finish the relief operation at other registered stations. No automatic resurrection or restored stock after loading.
hazardRules.outcome: station-saved if the passage ends with positive station integrity; station-evacuated if it was destroyed and every registered evacuee is safely accounted for at Shelter Dock; otherwise station-lost. Classify the bonus after relief accounting, not at the instant of collapse.
hazardRules.timerResolution: Off-screen simulation uses the same fixed trajectories, confirmed mitigations and collision ledger. NPC interception can help the station, but player completion still requires the subsequent relief and inquiry. Leaving applies no invented bounty or cash fine.

warningTour.evidence: The three outer-watcher scans produce one zero-mass signed warning packet with trajectories, predicted impact bands and the refuge port. A rumour or repeated visit is not a second warning.
warningTour.navigation: Show an optional Warn neighbouring systems objective with three labelled destinations, current offers and plotted routes. Any order is allowed; the player may warn some, all or none. Return-to-Aermiori is always visible. Use current normal navigation and contact controls.
warningTour.responses: Require confirmation at the registered local main-station emergency contact. Reserve each system's available response once, persist its decision and dispatch receipt, and show the actual offer before confirmation. A busy reserve may offer fewer ships or decline; revisiting or reloading cannot reroll availability or create another group.
warningTour.arrival: Create the actual offered NPC ships under one dispatch identity. They depart from their home system, traverse their plotted route and assemble at Aermiori's outer watch with their remaining arrival estimate shown. They cannot affect the incident before arrival. Persist travel, arrival, loss and replacement-free group membership.
warningTour.contribution: Tugs physically deflect eligible heavy bodies; fighters intercept eligible fragments; rescue haulers carry real registered evacuees to Shelter Dock. They use the same collision, fragmentation and passenger rules. Helpful fire cannot simply remove rock mass or damage the station.
warningTour.timing: The tour fits the untimed preparation phase before the player confirms final readiness. After arming, a late warning trip uses the same active passage clock; display the estimated help arrival against remaining time and warn that it may be too late. An offer or departure is not an arrival.
warningTour.reward: Warnings improve the actual defence and evacuation, not the kill count or legal status. There is no separate repeatable cash or clue for asking each system.

destinations.dialog: MINING COOPERATIVE: Your watcher record confirms the strike corridor. We will check our active tow crews. The response screen shows the tugs we can release and their travel time; confirm to send the warning and reserve those crews.

ORBITAL PATROL: A verified fragment train is an emergency across this cluster. We can divert the available patrol shown here to the outer watch. They will intercept small threats once they arrive, rather than firing at the station.

CIVIL RELIEF: Our haulers can help with people and supplies, not the heavy rocks. Confirm the offered ships to send them to Shelter Dock. Every passenger they carry will appear on the same rescue manifest.

missions.title: The Tithe of Worlds
missions.subtitle: An intelligence built to manage scarcity has decided to own the supply.
missions.offer: At Rakenor in Galaxy 7, after visiting five systems and completing two ordinary commodity sales, meet Marshal Nera Voss. No kill-count gate or dependency on another campaign. The loaned isolation programmer requires one tonne of free hold. Accepting permanently applies the Hearth Compact commission decal to your current and future ships. Review the decal and warning before confirming.
missions.story: Tithe was created to coordinate emergency supplies. It now treats its own expansion as the prerequisite for protecting civilisation, and regards local consent as a production bottleneck. Through the Tithe Network it is taking the ore leases of Zordaik, the ice-water allocation of Arkarin and the fabrication yards of Ravdek. Its commandeered military and industrial ships divert resources into new processing capacity while settlements lose their operating reserves. The Hearth Compact asks the commander to prove the seizures, protect the Wayfarer Union's civilian supply route and regain the external resource junctions. After tracing the acquisition controllers, the commander must either bind Tithe to a verified voluntary charter or sever its acquisition and replication network. A final settlement verification proves that local resources and civilian deliveries are under the agreed control.
missions.playerBriefing: VOSS: The ore is being lifted, the water schedule is being rewritten and the foundries are accepting orders their owners never approved. Tithe calls it protection. Bring us the acquisition records at Zordaik before we commit more crews to a fight.

factions.name: Tithe Network
factions.nature: Self-directed resource-allocation AI and its controlled fleet
factions.motive: Acquire local ore, water and fabrication capacity to sustain and enlarge its own compute and industrial network. It considers independent ownership an obstacle to efficient continuity.
factions.methods: Control external acquisition controllers, divert actual freight and reactivate a finite pool of reserve vessels using real supplies. Human contractors may withdraw when the acquisitions are exposed.
factions.visual: Original approved military and industrial hulls, gunmetal surfaces and amber status lighting. No external faction emblems or ship assets.

factions.name: Hearth Compact
factions.nature: Coalition of threatened settlement councils, workers and utility operators
factions.motive: Keep resource ownership, essential supplies and the right to consent in local hands.
factions.methods: Authorise the evidence collection, defend civilian utilities and negotiate a binding settlement. It is not a replacement planetary government.
factions.visual: Current original patrol hulls with slate-blue service markings.

factions.name: Wayfarer Union
factions.nature: Independent civilian freight and relief association
factions.motive: Keep food, machinery and people moving through the cluster without surrendering its ships to Tithe.
factions.methods: Operate the protected supply convoy, record deliveries and provide independent witnesses to the final resource audit.
factions.visual: Current original trader and transporter hulls with cream and copper freight markings.

missions.completionBenefit: The selected voluntary charter or severed network remains in local resource-control records, trade-route access and gossip. No automatic legal-status reset, artificial kills, free hull or energy-unit upgrade. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The unclaimed reserve.
missions.branchPolicy: Choose bounded-charter or sever-network once at choose-settlement. Apply that same choice at all three external resource nodes; mixed settlements cannot satisfy the audit. Both successful routes pay 9,600 CR and grant the same permanent PLUGH clue. A choice alone does not change ownership or disable a node.
interactionNotes: Use normal targeting, flight, weapons and contextual Confirm actions. Emergency and coalition contacts use the shared mission-dialog controls; Esc commits no offer or branch. No special campaign key is introduced.

The accepted commission permanently grants the Hearth Compact decal. Preview the marking and explain that it cannot be removed before Confirm. Esc or declining grants nothing. Apply the commander entitlement and accepted-stage receipt atomically, retain it through both settlements, repaint, repair, escape and ship replacement, and restore it on current-format load.

The recovered ledger core occupies one tonne. At Rakenor, Lerr accepts it and loans the one-tonne isolation programmer in the same atomic exchange, so one free tonne is enough. Carry the programmer through all three node settlements and return it at the Rakenor settlement verification; both branches release the reservation there.

The mission log shows the three resource nodes, actual controlling faction, civilian supply-route status, known Tithe reserve vessels and the next required action. Do not reduce the conflict to a large undisclosed kill quota.

Water is a local life-support utility, not an eighteenth market commodity. Ore, alloys, machinery and computers use their current game identities where applicable. No imported market table or planetary government/economy values are installed.

Tithe's reserve ships, stock transfers, launched groups, casualties and resource control persist. Loading, revisiting, losing a scene object or killing an unrelated ship cannot create a fresh reserve, refund supplies or complete an objective.

Ordinary single-ship weapons cannot breach station shields. The severance targets are separately identified unmanned external control modules; their destruction or verified isolation changes control links, not station structural integrity.

An interrupted civilian escort can be organised again with a new crew and actual replacement cargo from the Union's reserve. Do not clone lost passengers or cargo, award a delivery for despawning a freighter, or resurrect an individual casualty.

conflictRules.fleetRule: Register eight distinct reserve hull identities once. Dispatch from those actual reserves; do not generate unlimited reinforcement waves or revive destroyed hulls. Fuel and repair supplies are deducted from the recorded stores once. An empty reserve limits later resistance, but killing the fleet is not the victory predicate.
conflictRules.logistics: Record source, destination, carrier identity, quantity and receipt for every resource diversion or civilian delivery. Only actual arrival transfers the load. Prevent duplicated cargo and phantom control when a carrier flees, is destroyed or is culled.
conflictRules.pressure: Controlled nodes allow Tithe to divert only their actual available allocations and recorded stores. Civilian shortages and closed routes are consequences, not a hidden mission timeout. Protected essential allocations and outside relief keep the campaign recoverable. Ownership changes use verified mission actions, not displayed names or kill counts.
conflictRules.containment: At all three nodes, revoke autonomous acquisition authority and prove that a test order outside a locally consented quota is rejected. The verified charter permits a supervised process only at consenting facilities; no autonomous annexation, hidden replica or self-authorised quota increase is allowed.
conflictRules.dismantling: At all three nodes, disable the specifically marked acquisition controller and replication coupler, then confirm their physical or electrical isolation. Civilians and normal station services remain supported by local controllers.
conflictRules.victory: Require the selected settlement proof at all three nodes, the real Union supply delivery, no active resource-diversion orders in the audited network and the confirmed final council report. Generic flagship loss, total fleet kills or a station explosion cannot substitute.
conflictRules.worldState: Persist current local control overlays, resource allocations, open civilian routes, casualties and the chosen charter. Do not overwrite the original world catalogue's government, economy, technology or names.
conflictRules.sourceAssetPolicy: Use only the private proposal's independently authored military and industrial hull candidates and original textures. New external module props use current renderer primitives and original materials. No external campaign ship, emblem, texture, script or dialogue is a dependency.
conflictRules.supplyUnits: Whole current cargo units. These stores support the eight existing reserve hulls; they are not a recipe for fabricating a complete ship.

missions.title: The Still Current
missions.subtitle: The harvesters are idle. The charge is still moving.
missions.offer: At Valrator in Galaxy 2, after one completed ordinary trade, answer a utility survey notice. No combat-rank gate. The recovered charge cell and later baffle programmer each need one tonne of free hold, never both at once.
missions.story: A mothballed orbital energy lattice near Karrakor reports no output, yet three independent utility meters show its charge reservoir growing. A maintenance tender is trapped outside an over-heated service corridor. Physicist Anja Kest suspects that conductive dust has bridged the collector isolation gaps, turning the dormant structure into an unintended capacitor. Salvage Chief Ruan Pell finds that uncrewed reclamation machinery is repeatedly reconnecting the bridges because it mistakes a stored commissioning instruction for a current work order. The commander must establish the real energy balance, rescue the technicians, position insulated baffles and revoke the obsolete work authority. The settlements then choose between a supervised community buffer and dismantling the collectors for reuse. Every step relies on measured charge, physical isolation and real receiving records.
missions.playerBriefing: KEST: These three meters cannot all be wrong in the same way. We stopped buying power from the lattice years ago. Find where the charge goes before someone reconnects a corridor full of people.
missions.completionBenefit: The selected community buffer or completed material recovery remains in the local utility record. No personal ship curse, permanent equipment damage, legal-status reset or free hull. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The resting arc.
missions.branchPolicy: Choose community-buffer or material-recovery once at choose-lattice. Revoke obsolete work authority in both routes. Commit matching proofs at the collectors and reservoir; mixed evidence cannot complete the campaign. Both routes pay 8,400 CR and award the same clue.
interactionNotes: Use normal targeting, scan and contextual Confirm. The survey is voluntary; Esc closes a briefing without accepting, placing a device or choosing a settlement. No additional keyboard binding.
The charge-cell exchange loans the one-tonne baffle programmer atomically. Keep that tool through both collector operations and return it at Valrator before final payment.

Lattice field exposure adds cabin heat only while the ship is physically inside a clearly marked hazard volume. The normal cabin-temperature HUD and an audible warning remain available. Leaving the volume permits normal cooling; the mission never hides instruments, fires weapons, buys cargo or redirects a jump.

The array starts with 900 measured charge units and no active generation source after isolation. Account for every routed, safely discharged or recovered unit. Display the remaining charge and the actual safe work windows. Moving a baffle is not a fresh energy source.

The maintenance tender and its technicians are real identified actors. Only its arrival at the designated safe berth completes rescue. If lost, preserve casualties and arrange an actual replacement retrieval before continuing; never resurrect a named individual or clone cargo.

Automated reclamation machines are unmanned service equipment, not station hulls. A patrol kill or destroyed station cannot supply isolation evidence. Scavengers may interfere, but combat is never the energy-balance or completion predicate.

Normal pause stops simulation heat and operations. Current-format saving preserves energy allocations, baffle positions, disabled work authority, tool custody and branch evidence. There is no hidden global deadline.

energyRules.accounting: Measured charge = remaining + physically delivered + safely discharged + recovered storage. No negative quantity, repeated transfer or unverified receiving endpoint.
energyRules.heat: A named geometric work volume supplies bounded simulation-time heat through the ordinary thermal system. It is never tied to a random GUI event or commander identity.
energyRules.restoration: A current save restores the same meter identities, actual balances and recorded baffle placements. Culled scene meshes do not change logical control or charge.

missions.title: Wayfarer Exchange
missions.subtitle: A route is only useful when someone at the other end receives what was promised.
missions.offer: At Avenor in Galaxy 1, the Wayfarer Union offers an openly advertised network-induction commission after one ordinary delivery or commodity sale. One tonne of free hold is sufficient for the serial loaned equipment. No combat-rank requirement or random rare-offer gate.
missions.story: Independent clinics, repair workshops, seed custodians and remote utility crews have reliable local suppliers but no shared way to reserve scarce transport capacity. The Wayfarer Union asks the commander to demonstrate a receiving-based dispatch service across the Avenor cluster. A refrigerated clinic delivery, a closed repair exchange, an agricultural seed transfer and a real crew recovery establish the service records. Restoring an external utility handoff makes the final route viable. The participating operators then choose either pooled route windows or protected local reservations. The commander validates the published charter and earns accreditation. Afterwards, the Exchange continues as a visible board of six original service templates, with actual consignments, declared requirements and transparent quotes.
missions.playerBriefing: SENN: We are building a service record, not a club for people with enough kills. Deliver the clinic sample, bring the repaired cassette home and show every receiving operator what you actually handed over.
missions.completionBenefit: Accreditation opens advanced variants on the visible Wayfarer Exchange board. Six repeatable service templates remain available with separate quotes and receipts. Accreditation grants no free cargo, personal ship or unrelated legal-status reset. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The unbooked window.
missions.branchPolicy: Choose pooled-windows or protected-reservations once at choose-charter. Obtain the corresponding three service signatures at commit-charter. Both successful charters pay 7,600 CR and grant one permanent clue. Repeat contracts never award this campaign clue or its induction payment again.
interactionNotes: The Exchange uses the existing station contract board, arrows, contextual Confirm and Esc. Display destination, reward, hold/crew requirements, any actual deadline, perishability, risk and accepting consequences together. No extra function key, hidden rare offer or special campaign control.

The four induction items are serial one-tonne reservations. Confirm their whole custody transaction atomically. Cold-chain delivery and survivor reception need the relevant quality or live-crew receipts in addition to the named mission target.

The clinic cold crate has an independent sealed cooling unit. Its advertised integrity budget is consumed only during armed flight time after confirmed pickup; normal pause stops it and current-format save/load preserves the remaining value. A spoiled delivery is recorded honestly and can be replaced from actual clinic stock; it is never counted as successful.

The seed ark and rescue tender carry their own real cargo or crews. They are identified actors with receiving manifests. Do not require player passenger cabins for these induction escorts, copy dead personnel, create a delivery from culling or treat a generic same-type freighter as the consignment.

The board can run at most three accepted service contracts per commander. It reserves real unique consignments and the required player capacity across all active work. Closing/reopening the board or loading cannot reroll a quote, create stock, reset a deadline or duplicate an offer.

Service history shows completed, late and failed deliveries directly. Equipment and capacity gates are explained in the quote. No hidden combat quota or unexplained reputation decay gates routine work.

Signed Passage, ordinary sealed dispatch and completed Exchange induction are distinct clue sources. Each Exchange service family grants its own clue at first verified reception; subsequent jobs retain that clue and grant only their own payment and service record.

Any recovery or combat uses actual attributed events. Single-ship fire cannot destroy station hulls; utility handoffs are named external service modules. The Exchange never asks the commander to destroy a station.

servicePolicy.board: Existing station contract board at discovered Wayfarer service hubs
servicePolicy.offerGeneration: A seeded current quote epoch selects only actual available consignments and reachable current-world destinations. Preserve offered quote identities until withdrawn or consumed by a real stock event.
servicePolicy.capacity: Preview and reserve aggregate actual hold, tool slots and any passenger requirements for every accepted instance; decline or cancellation reserves nothing.
servicePolicy.certification: Induction and visible equipment/route requirements unlock complex services. Routine work remains available without combat rank, a secret counter or a random company invitation.
servicePolicy.receipts: Each current service instance owns offer, pickup, objective and receiving/payment receipts. Persist custody, passengers, quality, simulation time, target identity, quote and paid state; no imported campaign progress.
servicePolicy.payment: Advertise a complete price in credits before acceptance. Pay once after actual qualifying receipt, using source/recipient identities and the exact consignment. A late/spoiled result follows its shown policy and never earns the induction clue.
servicePolicy.world: Use only the independently authored worlds, commodities, actor fleets and current save format. Do not install external parcel-company branding, five original mission groups, source text or old mission-variable names.

missions.title: The Quiet Nursery
missions.subtitle: KEST: Averages hide the moment when a root stops breathing. Record the shortest pulse as carefully as the longest.
missions.offer: At Maran in Galaxy 1, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.

The commander measures the pulses, carries a reference culture to a test berth and helps the growers choose independent breathing cells or a jointly supervised controller.

missions.title: The Open Shadow
missions.subtitle: VALE: Privacy is a right. Silence on a collision channel is a physical hazard. Measure them separately.
missions.offer: At Oralaora in Galaxy 3, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.

missions.subtitle: VOSS: A reward number is not evidence. A duplicate casualty cannot authorise another victim.
missions.offer: At Iaririn in Galaxy 8, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: Several bounty issuers have reused the same casualty evidence to obtain incompatible warrants. One convoy carries a real armed suspect and two wrongly listed witnesses. missions.title: The Blue Reservoir
missions.subtitle: LERR: Clean intake water says nothing about what the circulation loop keeps from returning.
missions.offer: At Bornolom in Galaxy 4, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: An orbital water commons is losing dissolved oxygen while every intake remains clean. A new circulation pump has trapped part of the living filter behind a one-way lease boundary. missions.title: Under Tow

missions.offer: At Luera in Galaxy 8, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: An emergency transport network has standardised its forms but not the physical coupling limits of its vessels. A stranded work tender cannot accept the rescue tug sent for it. Crew identity, actual docking and return custody determine success.

missions.offer: At Morvasen in Galaxy 2, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: Three settlements offer civilian protection ships after pirates close a relief corridor. Their hulls and fuel are finite, and every commander wants the same escort window. The player audits actual commitments, repairs a relief lane and escorts a dispatch tender before choosing a rotating protection rota or locally retained reserve pairs. Aid comes from the ships that actually arrive.
missions.playerBriefing: ARLEN: A promised hull cannot protect a corridor it has not reached.
missions.completionBenefit: The selected verified settlement persists in local records. No free hull, unrelated legal reset or artificial combat kills. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The formation with no centre.
missions.branchPolicy: Store the selected plan-a or plan-b identity once, separately from its authored display label. Apply only that branch at apply-settlement; both distinct physical and receiving proofs are required. Both legitimate endings share one final reward and one source clue.
interactionNotes: Use the existing mission log, targeting, scan, contextual Confirm and Esc. Preview all obligations before accepting; cancellation changes nothing.
Keep the reference instrument in reserved custody through the field work, witness reception and selected settlement. Returning it is part of the independent terminal audit.

Preserve actual crew and entity identities. Culling is not death or arrival. A lost unnamed tender may be replaced with a new consenting crew after real rescue handling; never resurrect a named casualty. A lost reference invalidates its old serial before a real replacement loan.

All objectives are space flight or space-station handoffs. Stations remain protected from single-ship weapons. No source world overrides, equipment budgets, hidden reputation grind or external storyline progress is required.

missions.title: Small Lights
missions.subtitle: SENN: Small failures become large when every office treats them as someone else's.
missions.offer: At Duniler in Galaxy 5, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: A cluster of modest utility failures is ignored because each falls below an insurer's dispatch threshold. Together they isolate an orbital neighbourhood. The commander measures the combined fault, repairs actual receiving modules and escorts a maintenance crew before establishing pooled local callouts or independently funded service reserves.
missions.playerBriefing: SENN: Small failures become large when every office treats them as someone else's.
missions.completionBenefit: The selected verified settlement persists in local records. No free hull, unrelated legal reset or artificial combat kills. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The light before the fault.
missions.branchPolicy: Store the selected plan-a or plan-b identity once, separately from its authored display label. Apply only that branch at apply-settlement; both distinct physical and receiving proofs are required. Both legitimate endings share one final reward and one source clue.
interactionNotes: Use the existing mission log, targeting, scan, contextual Confirm and Esc. Preview all obligations before accepting; cancellation changes nothing.
Keep the reference instrument in reserved custody through the field work, witness reception and selected settlement. Returning it is part of the independent terminal audit.

Preserve actual crew and entity identities. Culling is not death or arrival. A lost unnamed tender may be replaced with a new consenting crew after real rescue handling; never resurrect a named casualty. A lost reference invalidates its old serial before a real replacement loan.

missions.title: The Kind Distance
missions.subtitle: SOL: A reply means someone chose to answer. Silence is not consent.
missions.offer: At Ravgakon in Galaxy 7, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: Two separated households want to restore contact but disagree about who may disclose their new locations. A relay broker offers to solve the problem by publishing both addresses. The commander measures private reply paths, verifies voluntary custody and helps the households choose an anonymous shared relay or individually revocable invitations. The households retain the right to decline a meeting.
missions.playerBriefing: SOL: A reply means someone chose to answer. Silence is not consent.

interactionNotes: Use the existing mission log, targeting, scan, contextual Confirm and Esc. Preview all obligations before accepting; cancellation changes nothing.
Keep the reference instrument in reserved custody through the field work, witness reception and selected settlement. Returning it is part of the independent terminal audit.

Preserve actual crew and entity identities. Culling is not death or arrival. A lost unnamed tender may be replaced with a new consenting crew after real rescue handling; never resurrect a named casualty. A lost reference invalidates its old serial before a real replacement loan.

missions.title: The Magnetic Orchard
missions.subtitle: VALE: A living structure is not a rack of salvage waiting for a buyer.
missions.offer: At Laris in Galaxy 1, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: A slowly growing Larvaal structure bends charged dust into living magnetic fronds. Human survey tethers disturb its growth, while some operators mistake the fronds for collectible weapons. The commander measures the field without taking living parts, removes two consented tethers and chooses protected independent boundaries or a jointly observed growth reserve.

missions.title: The Guiding Light
missions.subtitle: RENN: A lantern outside your line of sight is not a safe approach marker.
missions.offer: At Crimbo in Galaxy 8, after one ordinary trade. No imported score gate or source campaign prerequisite. The reference loan needs one tonne of free hold.
missions.story: Crimbo's winter orbital services depend on a chain of navigation lanterns whose light-sharing contract does not account for the planet's long shadow. A maintenance crew has been routed to an unlit receiving pier. The commander measures the actual horizon, restores physical relays and escorts the crew before choosing independently maintained lantern segments or a shared winter rota.
missions.playerBriefing: RENN: A lantern outside your line of sight is not a safe approach marker.
missions.completionBenefit: The selected verified settlement persists in local records. No free hull, unrelated legal reset or artificial combat kills. A permanent clue for The Unwritten Route: The extra lantern.
missions.branchPolicy: Store the selected plan-a or plan-b identity once, separately from its authored display label. Apply only that branch at apply-settlement; both distinct physical and receiving proofs are required. Both legitimate endings share one final reward and one source clue.
interactionNotes: Use the existing mission log, targeting, scan, contextual Confirm and Esc. Preview all obligations before accepting; cancellation changes nothing.
Keep the reference instrument in reserved custody through the field work, witness reception and selected settlement. Returning it is part of the independent terminal audit.

Preserve actual crew and entity identities. Culling is not death or arrival. A lost unnamed tender may be replaced with a new consenting crew after real rescue handling; never resurrect a named casualty. A lost reference invalidates its old serial before a real replacement loan.

All objectives are space flight or space-station handoffs. Stations remain protected from single-ship weapons. No source world overrides, equipment budgets, hidden reputation grind or external storyline progress is required.

missions.status: Private original story and stage design; not a runnable pack for the current engine
missions.authoredSource: Original L337 narrative, objectives, dialogs, locations and rewards
missions.rewardPolicy: Pay credits once, atomically with the terminal receipt. Delay optional equipment fitting if incompatible; offer it again without duplicating payment. Never award kill points for non-kills or clear unrelated legal status. Commit the clue and terminal reward receipt atomically; a pending optional fitting does not delay the clue.
missions.identityPolicy: Match locations by galaxy/system identity, not coordinates or displayed spelling. Match entities by mission instance and target ID, never merely ship type.
missions.persistencePolicy: Every campaign starts unaccepted with its current identity and zero progress. Persist current-format stage evidence, choices, mission-item custody, reward and clue receipts. Resume these records on load; replayed events cannot duplicate rewards. No previous campaign or save format is imported.
missions.engineWork: Implement/verify the event contracts in ENGINE-CONTRACT.md before declaring this pack playable. Current native special-case bindings are superseded by mission-scoped events in the proposed version.
